sentences.text: All the four appeals were heard together and are disposed of by this common judgment.

In brief the facts relating to the above four appeals are as under;
The West Bengal State Government issued a notification bearing No. 197-FS on 24.01.2014 empanelling 80 Flour Mills/Chakki Mills with their respective production capacity for the purpose of converting wheat into fortified Atta.

So far as Uttar Dinajpur, the effective production capacity of three flour mills per Metric Ton/Hour was rewarded as follows:

The District Controller (Food and Supply), Uttar Dinajpur by memo dated 17th October, 2014 reduced the effective production capacity so far as Raiganj Flour Mill from 6.5 MT/Hr and so far as Modern Dalkhola Modern Dalkhola Flour Mills Pvt. sentences.text: This reduction and enhancement as alleged by the writ petitioners was without any inspection or survey of the Flour Mills.

According to Raiganj Flour Mills State Government did not produce any document either before learned Single Judge or before the Division Bench to establish the basis upon which the reduction or enhanced production capacity of the respective parties was carried on.

Since no response whatsoever came to be made to the several letters pointing out grievances against the reduction of the capacity, the writ petitioner had approached this Court in W.P.7803 of 2015 challenging the action of the District Controller (F & S), Uttar Dinajpur in reducing the effective production capacity.

Apparently, the direction in the said writ petition on the State respondents was to conduct fresh inspection by competent authority to establish the correct effective production capacity of the writ petitioner and further that during pendency of such exercise, provisional allotment of 1 Metric Ton per hour should be continued.
Time limit was also made within which the competent authority had to comply with the said direction.

It was further made clear that in default of conducting above exercise in terms of the order within the specified period, the effective production capacity of the writ petitioner would be as specified by notification dated 5.7.2014 and the same shall be treated as valid.

This came to be challenged by Modern Dalkhola Flour Mills in an appeal contending that the writ petition filed by Raiganj Flour Mills was heard without hearing the affected parties which resulted in reduction of quota allocated to them.

Meanwhile, in terms of orders of Learned Single Judge dated 1.4.2015 after inspection and the report dated 26.5.2015 the effective production capacity of the writ petitioner was held to be 4.725 Metric Ton per hour.
When the matter came up before this Bench on 3.2.2016 a special inspection team was appointed.
The special committee report was placed on record on 8.2.2016 after inspection of all the Flour Mills.

According to appellant Flour Mills, so far as the allotment of 1 Metric Ton per hour as an interim measure till inspection was to be completed as directed by the learned Single Judge could not have been enhanced to 4.725 Metric Ton per hour in a contempt matter.

They further contended that the respondent authorities cannot modify or reduce production capacity of appellant Flour Mills to execute or implement an order in contempt Court when the records clearly indicate that the effective production capacity of the appellants was uniform at all material times and there was no such satisfactory information or material so far as Raiganj Flour Mill.

Subsequent to filing of the report of the special committee which made an inspection on 6.2.2016 of all the three Mills to ascertain their respective actual effective production capacity as on date clearly indicate the time of inspection of each of the Flour Mill, what exact observations were made by the inspection committee so far as each of the Flour Mill.
Exceptions to this report were placed by all the parties i.e three Flour Mills.

The special committee consisted of one Mr. Manu Chandra Barman,
Divisional Engineer Commercial, an officer in the rank of the Executive Engineer of Electric stream,
Mr. Durgadas Goswami, Secretary of C & I and Smt. Aparna Banerjee, Advocate.

The exercise of inspection of GMS Product (P) Limited started from 10.30 a.m. and the details are enumerated at paragraph 3 of the report which reads as under:

At para 5 it is stated that the inspection of the writ petitioner Flour Mill was commenced at 6.30 p.m. and up to 10.10 p.m., the committee was in the said Flour Mill.

The details are mentioned at para 5 of the report as under:
"5. The Committee thereafter started for Raiganj [located at a distance of approximately 45 km] and conducted inspection of Raiganj Flour Mill (P) Ltd starting from 6.30 pm.

The inspection was conducted in the presence of the committee members, Sri Jagadish Prasad Agarwal, Director, Sri Pankaj Saha,
Manager and other employees of the mill.
Initially the committee visited the entire complex of the mill, watched all the equipment and accessories, godown and the system of packaging through both manual and online automatic systems.

The Director showed the committee members the actual process of production of Atta through manual packaging system because he stated that online automatic packaging system was not run previously because no order/allotment of wheat was received from the Food and Supplies department and for that reason adequate number of machine operators were not appointed, and that is why he wanted to show the manual system.
Accordingly from shut down condition of all machines, all the running machines were restarted after ten minutes.
Original inspection report prepared in situ is enclosed herewith as Annexure-C.

From the inspection it transpires that production capacity, i.e production of Atta in bags @55 kg through manual packaging system was found to be 5.257 Metric Ton per hour generated out of mainly three manual packaging units.
One more manual packaging machine was found to be integrated with the system but was not functioning properly at the time of inspection.
Thereafter the said Director wanted to show also the production system through online automatic packaging system and he wanted some time to put the machines in order.
Time for fifteen minutes was granted initially.
On subsequent request time was further extended for one hour.

During this period of one hour one automatic machine could be started and it operated intermittently for about ten minutes and 572 packets of Atta @750 gm contained in each packet were generated out of the lone automatic online packaging unit.
But they failed to operationalize any other online automatic packaging unit and no attempt was also found to operationalize the other automatic online packaging units found on the floor.
The committee members wanted to know as to when the online automatic packaging machines were installed.
The Director of the mill stated that these were installed about one year back and the purchase vouchers are not readily available.
Therefore the committee decided to conclude inspection at 9.20 pm.
Then the report was prepared in presence of the Director and other employees of the said mill.
After having completed the report duly signed by the committee members and the Director and an employee of the mill, the committee left the mill premises at about 10.10 pm.
The entire process was video graphed and a few stull photographs were also taken."

Exceptions to the joint inspection report were filed on behalf of the writ petitioner Raiganj Flour Mill as well as Modern Dalkhola Flour Mill and GMS Product Private Limited.
Along with the inspection report of the committee, the notes prepared by the committee by hand is also placed.
The entire proceedings were recorded and the video CD is placed on record.

According to the writ petitioner so far as GMS Product Private Limited the milling capacity and packaging capacity of the Flour Mill alone was considered to arrive at conclusion that production capacity of the Mill is 4.137 Metric Ton per hour.
It is further said, in the absence of cleaning capacity of Flour Mill being inspected effective production capacity of the GMS Products as assessed by committee is vague.

So far as Modern Dalkhola Flour Mill, committee did not determine the cleaning capacity of the said Flour Mill per Metric Ton per hour, therefore based on milling and packaging capacity, the assessment of the committee regarding its capacity as 10.40 Metric Ton per hour is also vague.
They also contend that the report did not reflect notings made in the handwritten report i.e how many packets of Atta were produced by the other two Flour Mills through their automatic machines.
According to writ petitioner all the calculations are wrongly noted.

So far as the writ petitioner's Mill, except watching all the equipment accessories machineries, the members of the committee did not take inspection of cleaning capacity and only took inspection of milling capacity.

In spite of repeated request the team reluctantly took physical inspection of only one big automatic packaging machine and did not take inspection of the packaging capacity of the other big automatic packaging machine and rest seven small automatic packaging machines.
On the other hand, contrary to these exceptions, the report regarding Raiganj is much detailed and lengthier than the report pertaining to other two Flour Mills.
Jagdish Prasad, Director and Manager Pankaj Saha along with other employees were present.

The Director showed the production of Atta through manual packaging system and according to him online packaging system was not run previously since no order or allotment of wheat was received from the department, therefore, they did not have adequate number of machine operators hence he wanted to show the manual system.
All the running machines were restarted after ten minutes from shut down condition of the machines.
One more manual packaging was found to be integrated with the system but was not functioning properly at the time of inspection.
Apart from that, one manual packaging system was found to be working.

After spending more than one hour one automatic machine could be started and it operated intermittently for about ten minutes and 572 packets of Atta at 750 gm contained in each packet were generated from one automatic online packaging unit.
They did not operationalise any other online automatic packaging unit and no attempt was also made to operationalise other automatic online packaging units found on the floor.
According to the Director about one year back all the automatic packaging machines were installed but no material was placed.
The inspection concluded at 9.20 p.m.

sentences.text: Apparently, the contract demand of electricity of GMS is 350 KVA, Modern Dalkhola is 450 KVA and Raiganj is 126 KVA-.
With the above demand of electricity of all the three Flour Mills one has to ascertain whether the machineries found in the mills could be run at the same time.
One has to see whether in terms of the notification the entire process could be done in an integrated system without any human interference.
Packaging is on-line system (automatic) because consumption of fortified Atta by consumer should get benefit of fortified Atta (nutrients).
It has to go through the process in a systematic way from one stage to the last stage of each poly pack of 750 gm.

Cleaning,
milling and packaging operations have to be done in the Mill in terms of notification.
Whether manual packaging is allowed in terms of notification of 3.9.2013 also is to be seen.
The eligibility criteria is indicated in the above said notification wherein no Flour Mill with semi- automatic/manual packaging system would be considered is the stand of the appellants.
In terms of conditions indicated in the notification of 2013 each of the Flour Mill have to be considered for the purpose of allotment of wheat for conversion from wheat to fortified Atta.
Whether such conditions are complied with or not as per the report of the Special Committee constituted by this Court is to be seen from the report, hand written notes and also the contents of CD.

Eligibility criteria for selection of Flour Mills are clearly mentioned by the prescribed authority for conversion to fortified Atta which are as follows:
Kolkata, the 3rd September, 2013 Guidelines In supersession of the earlier guideline regarding introducing and running of Fortified Atta through PDS Vide No.
5 3 4 7 - F S / S e c t t / F o o d / 1 3 A - 0 6 / 0 7 D t . 1 0 . 0 8 . 2 0 0 7 a n d N o . 9 0 1 - FS/Sectt/Food/13A-04/2012, dt. 29.02.2012 and for streamlining the process of conversion of Wheat (BPL/APL) into wholemeal Atta/fortified Atta and smooth distribution thereof through PDS the following revised Guidelines shall take immediate effect in accordance with provision of the WB PDS (M&C) Control Order,
2013 and UPDS Control Order, 2013.
The Guidelines shall be applicable to the entire state covering MR & SR areas.

1. Eligibility Criteria for selection of Flour Mill(s):
i) In addition to the main Wheat Crushing Machinery, the Mill should be equipped with Cleaning Machine (for cleaning of Wheat before grinding), Dozing Machine (for premixing nutrients at appropriate dose) and Automatic Online Packaging Machine capable of packaging 750 grams and 500 grams of Atta in properly labelled Ploy packs having thickness above 40 microns (to avoid wastage, contamination, short weighment and proper sealing).
No Flour Mill with semi-automatic/manual Packaging machinery will be considered.
ii) The Mill should be capable of giving Atta at an out turn ratio not less than 95%.

Packaged product should conform to the specification laid down under Food Safety Modern Dalkhola Flour Mills Pvt. Ltd. & ... vs Raiganj Flour Mill (P) Ltd. & Ors on 15 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92047831/
7 and Standards (Food Products and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011 and IS: 1155- 1968.
iii) The selected flour mill(s) shall enter into an agreement with respective DCF&S/JDRs of Food &
Supplies Department, according to Proforma prescribed by the Government within 30 days from the date of offer, clearly mentioning the duration of Agreement.

iv) The Mill shall submit valid Bank Guarantee to the tune of 1.5 (one and a half) times of the economic cost of the allocated quantum of wheat as prescribed in the agreement in order to cover the difference between the market price and of the issue price of the allocated quantum of wheat.
v) The Director, DDP&S/D.R.W.B. will make normal monthly allotment of wheat to Flour Mills with prior approval of the Government.
vi) Monthly allotment to a particular Flour Mill will be based on the effective production capacity of the Mill and availability of wheat for a particular month.
This will form no basis of future claim of the Flour Mill.

vii) For the purpose of determining effective production capacity of a mill, the output generated from its packaging capacity, whichever is less, shall be considered for the purpose of allotment of wheat.

In case there is no/insufficient Roller Flour/Chakki Mill in a District or no Mill qualifies for selection, or operation of only existing running mill in a District is suspended or its agreement is terminated, the Director, DDP&S will select Flour Mill(s) from the adjoining District having the parameters spelt out in eligibility criteria.

The so selected Flour Mill in the adjoining district(s) will open outlets in the concerned District so that MR distributors of the district may lift wholemeal Atta/fortified Atta from the outlets within their district and the Roller Flour Mill(s)/Chakki Mill(s)
will not be entitled to any additional transport charges/operational cost etc for running these outlets.

3. After lifting of the stock of wheat (or after receiving it from the FCI) and crushing the same into wholemeal Atta which should not be less than 95% of Wheat, it should be fortified with micronutrients (e.g. Vitamin A, Fe (iron) & Folic Acid) in strict observance of the procedure laid down under the Micronutrients Initiative Project in case of fortified Atta scheme.
The fortified Atta should be packed into Ploythene packets having thickness of at least 40 microns and each packet should have 750 grams/500 grams of Atta as directed by the DCF&S/SCF&S.
Each packet will bear a printed label as prescribed by the department.
4. Wheat will be allocated on a fortnightly/monthly basis by the DCF&S/JDRs concerned to the Roller Flour/Chakki Mills.
The packaged Atta milled from one allocation shall constitute one batch.

5. Quality Control:-
i) Each Flour mill shall select a reputed independent Quality Control Firm/Agency for the purpose of quality certification of the flour produced by the mill as per standards specified by the Director of I & QC.

The role and function of such Firm/Agency shall be to do physical and chemical analysis of batch wise production, examine its conformity with specified standards and certify it, after which the batch will be sent for packaging.
There will also be sample checking of the packaged batch of Flour/Atta by such Firm/ Agency.
The Firm/Agency shall provide written certificate of fitness for consumption as packaged under hygienic condition and shall also give a copy of the same to the Directorate of I & QC.

Provided that such selected Agency/Firm in respect of Quality Control as offered by the Flour Mill shall be examined and vetted as to its suitability by the Director of I & QC and shall be engaged for not more than one year at a time which can further be renewed annually for another two years subject to satisfactory performance.

The qualification as to admissibility of independent Quality Control Agency shall be determined by the I & QC Directorate in keeping with the prevailing standards and infrastructure available with such Firm/Agency.
The name of proposed Firm/Agency shall be offered by the Mill within 30 days of receipt of its offer of engagement.

Provided further that a mill may like to change the selected Firm/Agency at any point of time stating reasons to the I & QC Directorate and replace it by another Firm/Agency subject to the process as mentioned in foregoing Paras.

The I & QC Directorate shall have overall supervision powers and authority to inspect flour mills at any point of the time, advise the independent Quality Control Agency, and take appropriate action if any irregularity is detected.
ii) "First in first out" system of wholemeal wheat/fortified Atta/Atta according to the date of production should be maintained strictly.

iii) Proper Hygienic condition of the Milling place, Online Packaging place, Storing places of Wheat,
wholemeal Atta & Fortified Atta should be maintained.
iv) Separate storage Godown for wheat and wholemeal Atta/ fortified Atta is mandatory.
v) Cleanliness of the milling equipments and devices at all points are to be maintained regularly.
Magnetic separator device, net/sleve and calibration of dozing box should be checked regularly.

7.

The selected Flour Mill(s) shall maintain stock of wheat received for crushing and the chemicals used for fortification as well as of packaged wholemeal Atta/fortified Atta separately to facilitate inspection and checking from time to time.

8. Distributors/whole sellers will obtain indents from the concerned SCF&S/R.O.s and lift the stock of wholemeal Atta/fortified Atta as the case may be, from the assigned Roller Flour Mill(s)/Chakki Mill(s) on deposition of money at the fixed rate to the said Mill.

The M.R. distributors/ Whole sellers/ WBECSE Ltd. will ensure door step delivery of Atta to dealers on deposition of money to them by the dealers for distribution to the BPL/APL beneficiaries at the prescribed price and at prescribed scale.
The Distributors/WBECSC Limited shall upload the lifting status online as directed by the department.

9. The selected Roller Flour Mill(s)/Chakki Mill(s) will inform the stock of unlifted wholemeal Atta/fortified Atta, if any, to the concerned DCF&S/JDRs within 3 (three) days from the last date of lifting.
The DCF&S/JDRs will review the situation and ensure that the entire unlifted stock of Atta is lifted and distributed among consumers within the month.
10. Unlifted Atta remaining with any selected Roller Flour Mill(s)/Chakki Mill(s) in a particular month will never be disposed of in open market.
The stock which could not be distributed within the month shall be carried forward to the next month and adjusted against the next month's allotment of wheat.
11. The wholemeal Atta/fortified Atta is to be distributed to the intended beneficiaries preferably within thirty (30) days from the date of milling.

12. Distribution of wholemeal Atta/fortified Atta will be through PDS channel only and as per provision of the WBPDS (M&C) order, 2013/WBUPDS (M&C) order, 2013 (as amended) and any violation of provisions of the order will result in imposition of Penalty under EC Act, 1955 (10 of 1955).

13. The Roller Flour/Chakki Mill to be selected shall install CCTVs and Cameras at the places of Milling, Packaging, Storage and Transportation points within one month from the date of offer for engagement.
14. Each selected Flour Mill/Chakki Mill shall keep record in authenticated register regarding the movement of traffic each day specially record of entry and exit of trucks in the Mill premises.

The colouring of storage Godown shall also be undertaken as per the specification given by the Department.
18. The selected Flour/Chakki Mill shall ensure Computerised Infrastructure as desired by the department as per the agreement.

19. The selected Flour Mill shall get the weighing devices (including weigh bridge) duly calibrated by the competent authority of the Government of West Bengal and shall keep the calibration certificate in the place of business for production on demand before Inspecting Officers.
20. The Flour Mill must obtain Fire Safety Certificate from the Fire Services Department and shall have to produce it during inspections.

21. Any person who is Proprietor/Partner/Director holding a M.R. Distributorship/Dealership Licence shall not be entitled to apply for selection of his Roller Flour/Chakki Mill in the above mentioned capacity under wholemeal Atta/fortification of Atta Scheme converted from wheat under BPL/APL scheme under P.D.S.
22.
If any irregularity comes to the notice of the department it is to be enquired into without any delay.

If it is found on inspection that serious irregularities has taken place on the part of any Flour/Chakki Mill, allotment of wheat will be stopped forthwith and penal action will be taken as per the law.

23. Whenever any action is taken as per para 22 against any Flour Mill, the allotted wheat for that particular mill will be distributed among the other neighbouring existing selected Flour Mills as per their capacity for uninterrupted supply of Atta under TPDS or as the department may deem fit.

sentences.text: The first eligibility criterion clearly indicates so far as packaging machine it should be automatic online packaging machine and so far as cleaning machine and dozing machine there is no indication of automatic machinery.
Even the thickness of the poly pack is clearly mentioned.
Depending upon the capacity of the production of fortified Atta through automatic online packaging machine the quantity of the wheat to be supplied will be decided.

It is also very clear that monthly allotment to a particular Flour Mill will be based on the effective production capacity of the Mill which again depends upon availability of wheat for a particular month.
Therefore, supply of particular quantity of wheat in a particular month cannot be a basis for claiming that for all time to come the supply of wheat must be of the same quantity.
The conditions therein clearly indicate quality control will be done by a reputed independent quality control firm or agency.
Any violation of terms and conditions would result in termination of contract.
The period of contract will be for one year which can be extended in terms of notification for another two years.
It is not one person committee which inspected the three Flour Mills concerned but three members from different walks of life are selected which includes one advocate as well.
Several deficits were pointed out by the respondent/writ petitioner contending bias against the committee members.
The notes of inspection (hand written and typed) and also perusal of the CD produced clearly indicate, there is no manipulation or concoction in preparing the report.
What is indicated in the visual recording is depicted in the report of the special committee.

In order to obtain supply of wheat for conversion into fortified Atta, the machinery indicated in the notification ought to have been in existence as on the date of consideration of the Mill for the purpose of empanelment in order to enter into an agreement in terms of the notification.
Apparently, the inspection report also indicates demand of electricity by the three Mills.
When exactly these machineries were established in respective Mills have to be substantiated by documentary evidence.
In order to have empanelment, the required effective production capacity must be in existence at the time of consideration for empanelment.
Now we are in 2016, three years after the above notification.

Since the matter is pending before the Courts right from 2015 we are of the opinion the effective production capacity of the three Mills shall be considered in terms of inspection of the committee conducted on 6.2.2016.
Accordingly, we set aside the impugned orders in the above matters.

The respondent authorities shall proceed with the matter in fixing the effective production capacity of each of the three Mills based on the inspection report placed on record which indicates the actual effective production capacity of each Mill.

None of the notifications indicating the effective production capacity of the Mill so also directions of the Court indicating the supply of wheat would come to the benefit of any of the Mills concerned.
The respondent authorities shall complete the exercise within two weeks from the date of communication of this order.
Accordingly the above appeals are disposed of.
(Manjula Chellur, Chief Justice) I agree.

(Arijit Banerjee, J.)

It has to go through the process in a systematic way from one stage to the last stage of each poly pack of 750 gm.
Cleaning,
milling and packaging operations have to be done in the Mill in terms of notification.
Whether manual packaging is allowed in terms of notification of 3.9.2013 also is to be seen.
In terms of conditions indicated in the notification of 2013 each of the Flour Mill have to be considered for the purpose of allotment of wheat for conversion from wheat to fortified Atta.
